search.label: Search extensions
search.source: Extensions come from Open VSX (open-vsx.org), the vendor-neutral registry of the Eclipse Foundation. Orkestr applies themes, icons, grammars, snippets and language servers; extension code never runs.
search.emptyHint: Try other words, or install a .vsix file you downloaded.

compat.title: Compatibility
compat.nothing: Nothing this extension contributes can be used by the Orkestr editor.
compat.code: Extension code (JavaScript) — never run by Orkestr

verified.label: Verified
verified.tooltip: Open VSX verified that this publisher owns the namespace

unverified.label: Unverified publisher
unverified.tooltip: Open VSX has not verified the owner of this namespace

installed.label: Installed extensions
installed.emptyHint: Find one on the Open VSX tab or install a .vsix file.

vsix.label: Full path of a .vsix file on this computer
vsix.hint: The archive is checked before it is unpacked: unsafe paths, links and oversized files are rejected.

lsp.approveTitle: Allow the language server {{name}} to run?
lsp.approveBody: It is a third-party program that runs with your user rights and reads this project. You approve it once; a changed program asks again.
lsp.failedTitle: The language server {{name}} is not working
lsp.needsProject: Open a project with a folder to allow or start language servers.

settings.title: Editor
settings.colorThemeHint: Applies to the code editor only; the Orkestr interface keeps its own theme.
settings.iconThemeHint: Icons in the Files panel and the editor tabs.
settings.noThemes: Install a theme or icon theme extension in the Extensions panel to choose it here.
settings.languageServersHint: Completion, hover, go to definition, references, rename, formatting and diagnostics in the Code panel. A server starts when you open a file of its language, after you allow it once.

vscode.hint: This extension runs fully in Orkestr's VS Code (VSCodium): install it there to use its commands and views.
vscode.missing: To use this extension fully, install VS Code (VSCodium) in the VS Code panel first.
